title_en: Why This Cargo Airline Broke 3 Decades Of Boeing Widebody Loyalty To Give Airbus 1 Order
title_zh: 为什么这家货运航空公司打破了30年的波音阔身忠诚度，给空客1个订单
summary: Analyzing why Atlas Air broke its all Boeing streak for the first time.
summary_zh: 分析为什么阿特拉斯航空公司首次打破了波音的全部纪录。
body_en: Why This Cargo Airline Broke 3 Decades Of Boeing Widebody Loyalty To Give Airbus 1 Order

Luke Diaz is a freelance military writer with experience with active duty experience in the US Navy as well as defense and industrial engineering. He is a former Naval Flight Officer who performed tactical air control on the carrier-based E-2 Hawkeye.

The global air freight industry has been struggling to fill the void since Boeing ended production of its iconic 747 jumbo jet in 2021. The world's largest operator of the 747 to this day remains Atlas Air . However, in a landmark change of course, the cargo carrier has invested in Airbus for the future of its fleet. On March 16, Atlas placed an order for 20 Airbus A350F next-gen air freighters, with options for 20, adding 20 more purchase rights in October.

Atlas not only has the most 747 freighters globally, but it also flies the four specialized Dreamlifter transports used by Boeing to ferry large 787 components between manufacturing sites around the world. Extended production and development delays surrounding Boeing's upcoming 777-8F variant of the 777X series carry much of the responsibility for driving this fleet diversification. The A350Fs are scheduled to replace 747s between 2029 and 2034 as Atlas is forced to retire the aging quadjets.

In the context of the global aerospace duopoly between Boeing and Airbus, Atlas' decision to order the Airbus A350F represents a massive blow to Boeing's historical dominance in the heavy cargo market. No modern twin-engine aircraft can perfectly replace a Boeing 747, meaning the A350F is a replacement in capability and economics. One of the 747's unique cargo features is its upward-swinging nose door. Given the imperfect solution, Atlas explicitly stated that the 777-8F remains an option in the future.

As of 2026, Atlas has 113 aircraft in its fleet. All of those are Boeing 747, 777, and 767 widebody cargo jets. Thanks to its unmatched reach, the carrier holds about 13% of the global widebody freighter fleet, making it the single largest heavy air cargo operator. Its single-manufacturer relationship with Boeing began in the early 1990s when Atlas employed the 747 jumbos as the foundation of international supply chains that would build its business model.

Atlas currently operates 59 747s, including the final production airframe ever built by Boeing. The fleet breakdown includes 35 older 747-400s, 14 advanced 747-8s, 23 767-300s, and 11 777s. Those twin-aisle jets are supplemented by eight converted 737-800 narrowbodies operated for Amazon's domestic shipping. Atlas also flies a specialized subfleet of the four 747-400 Large Cargo Freighters, known as Dreamlifters. This impressive all-Boeing flightline is why its shift to Airbus will have ramifications for the entire industry.
Atlas Simply Couldn't Wait On the 777X Forever

The mechanics behind the 777X delays explain why Atlas had to look elsewhere for its most urgent fleet modernization programs, and why a future Boeing partnership is still very probable. Atlas was unable to get the strict guarantees about delivery schedules from Boeing on the arrival of its first 777-8F jets due to the fact that it has not yet been fully certified by the Federal Aviation Administration.

Despite early estimates that the 777-8F would have its commercial debut in 2027, the schedule continues to slide to the right. The baseline passenger 777-9 has faced a decade of intense scrutiny, design modifications, and FAA flight-test halts. Because the 777-9's entry into service has slid into 2027, the 777-8F program was automatically pushed back. Current estimates peg its debut around 2029 or 2030.

Still, transitioning completely to Airbus would cost hundreds of millions in pilot training, duplicate tooling, and separate parts inventories. Thus, the air cargo juggernaut has intentionally structured its corporate strategy to leave room for the 777-8F to integrate into later rounds of fleet renewal campaigns. However, if Atlas exercises all of its options, the A350F will replace almost half of its Boeing lineup.

The Airbus A350F is slated to be the superior weight lifter, but it will also have less internal volume than the 777-8F. The 777-8F offers a significantly wider cross-section and more total main-deck volume, and once it is certified, adding it will be a straightforward transition for Atlas's massive pool of existing Boeing pilots. For e-commerce giants like Amazon Air or DHL, who Atlas flies for on many missions, cargo space is often about volumetric room rather than heavy weight.

Atlas will likely need the 777-8F to satisfy clients whose light packages "cube out" the smaller Airbus frame too quickly. Additionally, because of the 777-8F delays, the FAA recently threw Boeing a lifeline in the form of a special exemption. It allows for the continued building of up to 35 current-generation 777 Freighters past the strict 2027 or 2028 ICAO global emissions deadlines.

Speculation within the cargo industry strongly indicates that Atlas is actively positioning to take a major slice of these 35 exemption slots. If Atlas acquires these bridge aircraft, it will form a renewed decades-long relationship for the 777 line that could seamlessly evolve into 777-8F orders when those airframes eventually age out.

One of the unique reasons the 747 Freighter became an industrial icon is because its entire nose section hinges upward. Combined with an elevated cockpit design, it enables straight-in, linear loading along the entire length of the main deck, which is very useful for outsized cargo. Oil and gas industrial ventures and defense contracts make up a large portion of the regular business for heavy air freight.

The absence of a nose-loading door on both the A350F and the 777-8F is shaping up to be a kind of crisis for the global cargo market in support of these sectors. The core problem with an all-side-door fleet is the 90-degree turn to the main deck. Cargo like an oil drill or a helicopter that easily slides straight into a 747 will be blocked against the opposite wall of a 777-8F or A350F before it can make the turn.

Since neither aircraft can replace the nose door, Atlas is likely positioning itself to use a mixed fleet of both the A350F and the 777-8F that will leverage the unique structural advantages of each to mitigate the loss of the 747's nose door. Airbus engineered the largest main-deck cargo door in commercial history for the A350F. It is 15% wider than previous-generation jets to accommodate the kind of massive items that required nose-loading in the 747.
body_zh: 为什么这家货运航空公司打破了30年的波音阔身忠诚度，给空客1个订单
Luke Diaz是一名自由撰稿人，在美国海军以及国防和工业工程方面拥有现役经验。他是一名前海军飞行军官，对舰载E-2鹰眼进行了战术空中控制。
自波音于2021年停止生产其标志性的747大型喷气式飞机以来，全球航空货运业一直在努力填补这一空白。迄今为止， 747的全球最大运营商仍然是阿特拉斯航空。然而，在具有里程碑意义的变化中，这家货运航空公司为其机队的未来投资了空中客车。3月16日，阿特拉斯订购了20架空客A350F下一代航空货机，其中20架有选择权， 10月份又增加了20架购买权。
Atlas不仅拥有全球最多的747货机，而且还运送波音使用的四种专门的Dreamlifter运输机，在世界各地的制造工厂之间运送大型787零部件。围绕波音777X系列即将推出的777-8F型号的延期生产和开发，在推动这一机队多元化方面承担了很大责任。A350F计划在2029年至2034年之间取代747 ，因为Atlas被迫退役老化的四缸喷气式飞机。
截至2026年，阿特拉斯拥有113架飞机。所有这些都是波音747、777和767宽体货机。凭借其无与伦比的覆盖范围，该航空公司拥有全球宽体货运船队约13%的份额，使其成为单一最大的重型航空货运运营商。阿特拉斯与波音的单一制造商关系始于20世纪90年代初，当时阿特拉斯将747巨型客机作为建立其商业模式的国际供应链的基础。
Atlas永远等不及777X了
777X延误背后的机制解释了为什么阿特拉斯不得不在其他地方寻找其最紧迫的机队现代化计划，以及为什么未来的波音合作伙伴关系仍然非常可能。Atlas在首批777-8F喷气式飞机抵达时无法获得波音公司对交付时间表的严格保证，因为它尚未获得联邦航空管理局的全面认证。
尽管早期估计777-8F将在2027年进行商业首次亮相，但进度继续向右滑动。基线乘客777-9面临十年的严格审查，设计修改和FAA飞行测试暂停。由于777-9投入使用已推迟到2027年， 777-8F计划被自动推迟。目前的估计在2029年或2030年左右首次亮相。
尽管如此，完全过渡到空中客车公司将花费数亿美元进行飞行员培训、重复工具和单独的零件库存。因此，航空货运巨头有意构建其企业战略，为777-8F整合到后几轮机队更新活动中留出空间。然而，如果阿特拉斯行使其所有选择权， A350F将取代其近一半的波音产品线。

title_en: Flying Blue Delays SAF & Donation XP Changes Until December 2026
title_zh: 蓝天飞行将SAF和捐赠经验的变化推迟到2026年12月
summary: Flying Blue is delaying until December 1, 2026 its 50% higher cost for earning XPs through SAF and mileage donations, after a rollout that caught members off guard.
summary_zh: 蓝天飞行计划将推迟到2026年12月1日，在推出该计划后，通过SAF和里程捐赠赚取经验的成本提高了50 ％
body_en: One unique aspect of the Air France-KLM Flying Blue program has long been how environmental contributions have contributed toward elite status, whether through the purchase of sustainable aviation fuel (SAF), or through mileage donations to environmental causes.

A couple of days ago I covered how seemingly overnight, the Flying Blue program drastically decreased status qualification through these methods , requiring 50% larger contributions to earn the same number of XPs (experience points, the method by which one earns status ). There’s now an update, and I’m pleased to see the way this is being handled.
Flying Blue pauses changes to XP earning from SAF

Flying Blue has announced that it’s delaying the changes it’s making to the ability to earn XPs through SAF and mileage donations, and this will now be implemented as of December 1, 2026. Tiffany Funk, Head of Flying Blue, shared the following with me

On Monday, we updated how many XP you earn on Sustainable Aviation Fuel and charitable contributions. We didn’t handle the rollout well, and the new rate went live with unclear messaging and without notice. While this affects a small share of our members, we recognize for those members it matters a great deal.
The update was part of a continuous review of our elite program. We want to ensure we can keep delivering the benefits and service you expect.

For now, we’re pressing pause. From tomorrow (4 November), SAF and charitable contributions will earn XP at the previous rate, and any contribution made since 2 November will be credited at the prior rate as well. The new rate of €15 per XP begins on 1 December 2026; even at the new rate, no program in the market will recognize SAF contributions more generously than Flying Blue, including on award tickets.

We want Flying Blue to be a program you build your life around. Many of you put a lot of care into planning your flights and status qualification, and we understand your need to have time to make adjustments.
And to everyone who told us why this matters to you: thank you for caring this much about Flying Blue.
This is the right way to handle this situation
I am happy to see how Flying Blue leadership is handling this situation. Let me share my take on this situation, broadly.

I don’t necessarily think Flying Blue had to make some big, public announcement about the change in advance. After all, this isn’t an official part of the program, and there has really never been any member communication about these opportunities.

I think what was frustrating is that the change was implemented before the website was even updated. So you had the higher pricing already showing, while the page about SAF and mileage donations still reflected the old cost, leaving many people wondering if the change was a glitch or intentional.
At a minimum, I think it’s appropriate to update the webpage before the changes go live, and ideally even give a little notice on the page dedicated to this, just so members aren’t caught off guard.

When it comes to the change as such, Flying Blue does indeed have the most generous opportunities to qualify for elite status through these types of contributions. Selfishly I love this option, but it’s not like members are “entitled” to a certain rate of qualification through this method, since there’s not actually any objectively “fair” way to reward elite qualification for contributions.
So for Flying Blue, it’s presumably about balancing environmental goals with elite ranks. I know with the 50% price hike, I’ll be much less likely to buy SAF, and that’s fine.

As of December 1, 2026, the Air France-KLM Flying Blue program will be decreasing the number of XPs that members earn for contributing toward sustainable aviation fuel and environmental causes. This was initially supposed to be implemented a couple of days ago, but members were caught off guard, so I appreciate that the implementation of this has been delayed.

Aircraft leasing company Avolon has finalized an order for 140 Boeing 737-10 aircraft, marking the largest-ever 737 MAX purchase by a lessor. The agreement increases Avolon’s total 737 MAX backlog to more than 240 aircraft. The order reflects growing demand among leasing companies for larger single-aisle aircraft. Lessors have placed firm orders for more than 230 Boeing 737-10s in 2026, five times their combined backlog for the variant at the end of 2025.

The Boeing 737-10, the largest member of the 737 MAX family, can accommodate up to 230 passengers and has a range of 3,100 nautical miles (5,740 kilometres). Boeing says the aircraft offers the lowest per-seat operating costs of any single-aisle aircraft.
According to Boeing, lessors have now ordered more than 1,450 737 MAX aircraft, representing approximately 20% of the manufacturer’s total backlog.

Condor has inaugurated a daily service from Frankfurt to Bangkok via Abu Dhabi, operated in codeshare with Etihad Airways. The new route complements its existing daily non-stop Frankfurt–Bangkok service, giving passengers two daily travel options between the cities.

The service uses Airbus A330neo aircraft and expands Condor’s winter offering to Thailand while strengthening its partnership with Etihad. The inaugural departure received a ceremonial send-off in Frankfurt, with an arrival ceremony also planned in Abu Dhabi.

Beyond Bangkok, the codeshare partnership provides connections through Abu Dhabi to destinations across Etihad’s network in Asia, Africa and Australia. Passengers can book connecting journeys on a single ticket and have their baggage checked through to their final destination.

Home Airports Bogota Airport (BOG) Qatar Airways launches Bogotá and Caracas service with Boeing 777-200LR

Qatar Airways has inaugurated a twice-weekly service linking Doha with Bogotá and Caracas, adding Colombia and Venezuela to its network. Operated by Boeing 777-200LR aircraft, the triangular route brings the airline’s presence in the Americas to 17 destinations.

Flights operate on Wednesdays and Sundays under flight number QR783, travelling from Doha to Bogotá, continuing to Caracas and then returning to Doha. The routing provides a non-stop outbound connection from Doha to Bogotá and a non-stop return from Caracas to Doha; passengers travelling from Doha to Caracas stop in Bogotá.

The airline says the schedule offers connections through Hamad International Airport to destinations including Australia, China, Japan and South Korea. Its winter network covers more than 170 destinations worldwide.

The launch also follows an expansion of Qatar Airways’ partnership with LATAM to include LATAM Airlines Colombia. Qatar Airways plans to place its code on LATAM-operated services connecting Bogotá with 17 Colombian destinations, including Medellín, Cartagena, Cali and San Andrés, extending onward travel options beyond the capital.

title_en: 7 Airlines With The Largest Dreamliner Fleets In 2026
title_zh: 2026年拥有最大梦幻客机机队的7家航空公司
summary: From launch customer roots to recent bulk orders, these airlines leverage Dreamliner commonality and size options.
summary_zh: 从推出客户根源到最近的批量订单，这些航空公司利用梦想飞机的通用性和尺寸选项。
body_en: An aviation writer, pilot, and flight operations professional who sees aviation from both sides of the cockpit door. With a background in aeronautics, safety, and human factors, she brings curiosity, firsthand experience, and a love of the details that turn aircraft and airports into stories worth telling.

The Boeing 787 Dreamliner has become an important aircraft for airlines operating long-haul services, offering a family of twin-engine widebodies designed for different passenger capacities and route requirements. Since entering commercial service in 2011, the aircraft has been adopted by carriers around the world, with the 787-8, 787-9, and 787-10 offering different combinations of capacity and range. These three variants let airlines choose aircraft that better match their network strategies without relying on a single widebody configuration.

The world's largest Dreamliner operators demonstrate how extensively the aircraft family has been adopted across Asia, Europe, the Middle East, and North America. This ranking compares seven airlines by their reported active Boeing 787 fleets, rather than combining aircraft already in service with future orders or scheduled flight volumes. Fleet registers can differ because of reporting dates and aircraft status, so the figures below should be read as reported late-2026 snapshots rather than permanently fixed totals.
A two-variant fleet of 42 serves different capacity needs

Japan Airlines operates a substantial Boeing 787 Dreamliner fleet, with approximately 42 aircraft listed in the available register snapshot. The Japanese carrier uses the 787-8 and 787-9 across its network, giving it two capacity options within the same aircraft family. This combination supports different passenger needs without requiring the airline to operate every Dreamliner variant.

The 787-8 offers a smaller-capacity widebody option, while the 787-9 provides additional space for passengers and cargo. Operating both models gives Japan Airlines flexibility when planning services with different levels of demand, although aircraft assignments also depend on route length, scheduling, and operational requirements. The shared aircraft family provides commonality while retaining meaningful differences in passenger capacity.

Japan Airlines ranks seventh in this comparison because its reported fleet is smaller than those of the other six operators featured here. Its Dreamliners remain an important part of the airline's widebody operation, particularly as the carrier balances capacity across its network. The reported total represents a fleet-register snapshot, and should not be interpreted as the total number of Dreamliners Japan Airlines has operated throughout the aircraft program's history.
43 total Dreamliners with three variants support long-haul operations

British Airways operates 43 active Boeing 787 Dreamliners, placing it sixth in this ranking. The aircraft form part of its long-haul fleet alongside other widebodies, including the Boeing 777 and Airbus A350. British Airways operates the 787-8, 787-9, and 787-10, giving it access to all three main production variants of the Dreamliner family.

The 787-8 is the smallest member of the family, while the 787-9 offers additional passenger capacity and the 787-10 accommodates even more passengers. These differences give British Airways several aircraft configurations to consider when planning long-haul services with varying demand . Operating three variants allows the airline to select among different capacity options without depending exclusively on one Dreamliner model.

British Airways' reported fleet is slightly larger than Japan Airlines' in this comparison, but smaller than those of Etihad Airways, Qatar Airways, American Airlines, ANA, and United Airlines. The Dreamliner complements the airline's other widebodies, each with its own role in the wider fleet. Its position here reflects reported active aircraft rather than additional Dreamliners that remain on order.
With 47, the 787-9 makes up most of Etihad's fleet

Etihad Airways operates 47 active Boeing 787 Dreamliners from its base in Abu Dhabi, placing it fifth among these seven airlines. Its fleet comprises the 787-9 and 787-10, which support international services across the carrier's network. The Dreamliner operates alongside other widebody aircraft, giving Etihad several aircraft options for routes with different passenger volumes and operating requirements.

The 787-9 makes up most of Etihad's Dreamliner fleet, with 37 active aircraft reported alongside ten examples of the larger 787-10. The 787-9 combines long-range capability with passenger capacity suited to a variety of international routes, while the 787-10 offers additional seating capacity. Together, these variants give the airline different options for matching aircraft size to route demand.

Etihad's 47 active Dreamliners put it ahead of Japan Airlines and British Airways, but behind Qatar Airways and the three largest fleets in this ranking. Its fleet composition shows a clear preference for the 787-9, while the 787-10 provides a higher-capacity option within the same family. The reported active-aircraft count is separate from scheduled flight totals, which measure planned operations rather than the number of aircraft operated.
A large fleet of 61 Dreamliners and a major future order

Qatar Airways operates 61 active Boeing 787 Dreamliners as part of its international network from Doha. The airline uses the 787-8 and 787-9, providing two capacity options within its widebody fleet. These aircraft complement other types, including the Boeing 777 and Airbus A350, giving Qatar Airways a broader range of aircraft for different routes and passenger requirements.

The 787-8 provides a smaller-capacity configuration, while the 787-9 offers additional space for passengers and cargo within the same aircraft family. Qatar Airways' reported fleet includes 32 active 787-8s and 29 active 787-9s, with another 787-9 listed as on order in the available register. This mix gives the airline flexibility when assigning aircraft across its international network.

In May 2025, Qatar Airways announced an agreement covering up to 210 widebody aircraft, including 130 Boeing 787 Dreamliners. Boeing described the 787 portion as the largest Dreamliner order in its history, underlining the scale of the airline's future fleet plans. These aircraft are not part of the current active fleet total, however, and should only be counted as they are delivered and enter service.

body_en: James lives and breathes route development. Educated in Air Transport Management at Loughborough University and Cranfield University, James has a PhD in Airline Strategy and Economics. James was Market Opportunity Analyst at London Luton Airport and Chief Analyst at anna.aero. He taught airline strategy and economics to undergraduate and postgraduate students for five years and has worked closely with multiple carriers on route and market intelligence projects. He is based near London, UK.
From now onwards, American Airlines plans 10 new or returning routes on the Boeing 777. Five are international and obviously long-haul, while five are domestic, mainly, but not always, between hubs.

American is the world's fourth-largest operator of passenger Triple Sevens. Ch-aviation shows that the oneworld member has 67 airframes: 47 777-200ERs (273 seats) and 20 777-300ERs (304 and 330 seats). The type comprises virtually half of American's widebody fleet (49%).
These Five New International Routes Will See American's 777

Schedule analysis using Cirium Diio data for November 2026 onward shows that these five new international routes will all see the 777, all on the 273-seat 200ER. They're from three major hubs: Charlotte Douglas International Airport (CLT), Dallas/Fort Worth International Airport (DFW), and New York's John F. Kennedy International Airport (JFK).

Perhaps the most notable addition is CLT to Barcelona. This is Spain's second most popular city, an enormous tourist destination, and a major location for cruises across the Mediterranean. It is also the country's primary industrial city, known for manufacturing (including cars) and so on. Historically, it was known as the Manchester of the Mediterranean.

Inherited from US Airways, from which American obtained the CLT hub (and also Philadelphia and Phoenix), flights from CLT to Barcelona will deploy the 777 for the first time in eight years. title_en: 5 Boeing 787-9 Fleets With At Least 40 Business Class Seats

summary: Five Boeing 787-9 business-class cabins stand out, but which airlines offer the most premium seats on their Dreamliners?

body_en: 5 Boeing 787-9 Fleets With At Least 40 Business Class Seats

Passionate about promoting aviation, the beauty of flight and the science behind it, Antonio is an avid reader of aviation magazines and books, and he loves visiting airshows all over the world, taking photos and writing about airplanes and helicopters as well. He is currently based in Palermo, Sicily.

The Boeing 787-9 is often associated with long-haul efficiency, but its business-class cabins can offer remarkably different experiences. Depending on the airline, passengers may find themselves in a relatively conventional layout or a spacious suite with a sliding privacy door. As AwardLocker’s comparison of business-class cabins highlights, the aircraft model alone reveals very little about what awaits behind the boarding door. For travelers choosing a long-haul flight , those differences can make one 787-9 considerably more appealing than another. Some airlines have gone particularly far in dedicating cabin space to business class, with configurations that stand out even among widebody aircraft .

This list examines five carriers operating Boeing 787-9s with at least 40 business class seats, comparing their layouts, seating products, and approach to premium travel. The order follows the number of business class seats, but the figures alone do not tell the whole story. And one configuration in particular raises an interesting question about just how much of a Dreamliner 's cabin an airline is willing to reserve for its most valuable passengers.
The smallest business cabin on the list, built for the longest flights

Qantas ’ 236-seat 787-9 has 42 business seats in a 1-2-1 layout, each with direct aisle access. Australian Aviation reported that the cabin also includes 28 premium economy seats and 166 economy seats. The first of Qantas’ 787-9s arrived in October 2017, and the business seat is the Thompson Aero Vantage XL, an evolution of the suite Qantas already flew on its Airbus A330 s. Business Traveller’s review adds that the 42 seats are split between a 30-seat forward cabin and a 12-seat secondary cabin, with a galley and lavatories in between.

Business class accounts for about 18% of the aircraft's total capacity, a relatively modest share compared with the other configurations in this countdown. Simple Flying examined how the 787-9's range lets Qantas operate long-haul routes directly from Australia instead of relying as heavily on hubs such as Singapore and Hong Kong. The aircraft also allows the airline to match capacity to demand without needing to fill an Airbus A380 , which matters when a jet has so few seats to sell. It is a small business cabin with big ambitions, designed for passengers who can spend most of a day in the air.

Qantas is not standing still. AwardLocker notes that the airline advertises an evolved suite with a sliding door for new 787-9 deliveries from fiscal year 2028. Simple Flying examined how the carrier is reshaping its fleet without grounding. Today's Qantas suites have no doors, so the upgrade represents a significant change to the passenger experience. Still, 42 seats are enough to make the aircraft a serious long-haul proposition. The next airline takes that premium investment further, with a cabin that offers considerably more personal space.
4 ANA’s 787-9 With The Room FX: 48 Business Seats

All Nippon Airways ' 206-seat 787-9 layout has 48 business seats in The Room FX. According to ANA , the seats alternate between forward- and rear-facing positions, and each is self-contained, with a door and a large 24-inch (61 cm) 4K monitor. ANA says it is the largest business class seat for a mid-sized aircraft, KarryOn reported , and the seat was developed with Safran Seats and Acumen. Pre-reclining the seat creates a sofa-like position, while adjustable leg rests turn it into a bed. The Points Guy adds that the 48 pods are split between the forward and rear cabins, with six rows each.

The dimensions help explain the attention surrounding the product. AwardFares reported a bed length of 76.5 inches (194 cm) and a waist width of 27 inches (69 cm), while Aircraft Interiors International says the sofa end is 41.5 inches (105 cm) wide. The same report adds that each of the 48 seats has a door, and that ANA plans a gradual rollout from 2026 on major long-haul routes. In effect, the seat offers more living space without adding weight, a clever trade for a mid-sized jet. Business class accounts for roughly 23% of the aircraft's 206 seats, giving the premium cabin a substantial share of the available capacity.

There is an important catch, however: not every ANA 787-9 has The Room FX. ANA’s cabin pages show that its 215-seat and 246-seat 787-9s use the Business Staggered seat instead, which also gives every passenger direct aisle access. ANA's cabin pages list each option by aircraft layout, so identifying yours takes only a minute. Checking the seat map before booking is essential, particularly when the difference between configurations can change the entire experience. With 48 business seats, ANA has already moved well beyond Qantas' more restrained layout. The next airline, however, manages to fit even more premium seats into its Dreamliner.
Search by where it's flying from and to. No flight number needed.
Or try: London → New York Heathrow departures British Airways
3 American Airlines’ 787-9P: 51 Business Seats
The premium Dreamliner with a door on every seat

American Airlines ' premium-heavy 787-9P has 51 business seats, made up of eight Flagship Suite Preferred seats and 43 standard Flagship Suites, all with doors, according to The Points Guy . The eight Preferred seats sit in the front row of each of the two business cabins. To keep the layout efficient, View From The Wing reports that the pitch is 42 inches (107 cm) at the windows and 44 inches (112 cm) in the center seats.

The Preferred suites offer up to 19% more bed space and 42% more living area, per AirlineGeeks . The whole aircraft seats 244, which makes business class about 21% of the cabin. Simple Flying explains that the premium-heavy version's forward mini-cabin offers the most exclusivity. Simple Flying also compared American's new Flagship cabin with United Polaris , a rivalry that is shaping US long-haul travel.

American also gives the 787-9P 32 premium economy seats, so the premium cabins together hold 83 seats. AwardWallet’s onboard measurements put the entertainment screens at 17.5 inches (44 cm), competitive with other US carriers, and every seat offers wireless charging.

title_en: FAA orders Boeing 787 fuel tank inspections over lightning strike explosion risk
title_zh: FAA 因雷击爆炸风险下令波音 787 油箱检查
summary: The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has ordered inspections of certain Boeing 787 Dreamliners after discovering that required manufacturing… The post FAA orders Boeing 787 fuel tank inspections over lightning strike explosion risk appeared first on AeroT
summary_zh: 美国联邦航空管理局 (FAA) 在发现需要制造后，已下令对某些波音 787 梦想飞机进行检查……
body_en: The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has ordered inspections of certain Boeing 787 Dreamliners after discovering that required manufacturing checks of fuel tank sealant were not completed or could not be verified, raising concerns about a potential fuel tank explosion during a lightning strike.

The FAA airworthiness directive (AD), published November 2, 2026, applies to certain Boeing 787-8, 787-9 and 787-10 aircraft. The FAA estimates that 60 US-registered aircraft are affected. The directive takes effect December 7, 2026.
The problem involves sealant installations inside the center wing fuel tank that lacked evidence of required visual and adhesion inspections during production.
The FAA warned that defective sealant could allow an ignition source to develop inside the tank during a lightning strike, potentially igniting fuel vapors.

“The unsafe condition, if not addressed, could result in development of an ignition source within the fuel tank volume and a risk of a fuel tank explosion during a lightning strike event,” the FAA said.

Under the directive, operators must carry out detailed inspections of sealant installations in the left, right and center wing side-of-body areas, including sections between the side-of-body rib and rib 2. The work includes checking for sealant defects, surface depressions and inadequate adhesion.
Any defects identified during the inspections must be addressed through approved repairs. The required work follows instructions contained in a Boeing requirements bulletin issued November 5, 2025.

The FAA estimates the AD inspections and adhesion tests will require approximately 34 hours of work per aircraft, costing $2,890 each. The total estimated cost for the 60 affected US aircraft is $173,400, excluding any repairs.
The agency said it lacked sufficient information to estimate the cost of corrective work that might be necessary if defects are discovered. Some expenses could be covered under Boeing’s warranty.
The directive follows an FAA proposal published February 24, 2026. During the public comment period, Boeing and American Airlines requested changes to the repair requirements.
Boeing asked the FAA to allow repairs using existing approved procedures, rather than requiring separate approval for each repair. The FAA agreed.

American Airlines asked the FAA to clarify where the sealant needed to be tested and whether existing Boeing repair procedures could be used. The FAA clarified the inspection areas and agreed to allow the existing repair procedures.
The Foundation for Aviation Safety separately asked whether Boeing was now performing the required sealant inspections during production.

The FAA said the directive covers aircraft for which there was insufficient evidence that the inspections had been completed. It confirmed that the required inspections are being performed during production on aircraft outside the directive’s scope.
The post FAA orders Boeing 787 fuel tank inspections over lightning strike explosion risk appeared first on AeroTime .
body_zh: 美国联邦航空管理局 (FAA) 在发现所需的油箱密封剂制造检查未完成或无法验证后，已下令对某些波音 787 梦想飞机进行检查，引发了人们对雷击期间可能发生油箱爆炸的担忧。
2026 年 11 月 2 日发布的 FAA 适航指令 (AD) 适用于某些波音 787-8、787-9 和 787-10 飞机。 FAA 估计有 60 架在美国注册的飞机受到影响。该指令于 2026 年 12 月 7 日生效。
该问题涉及中心翼油箱内的密封剂安装，缺乏生产过程中所需的目视和附着力检查的证据。
美国联邦航空局警告说，有缺陷的密封剂可能会在雷击期间在油箱内产生火源，从而可能点燃燃油蒸气。
美国联邦航空局表示：“如果不解决这种不安全情况，可能会导致油箱内产生点火源，并在雷击事件中存在油箱爆炸的风险。”
根据该指令，运营商必须对左、右和中翼机身侧面区域的密封剂安装进行详细检查，包括机身侧面肋和肋2之间的部分。工作包括检查密封剂缺陷、表面凹陷和粘合不足。
检查期间发现的任何缺陷必须通过批准的维修来解决。所需工作遵循 2025 年 11 月 5 日发布的波音要求公告中包含的说明。
FAA 估计每架飞机的 AD 检查和附着力测试将需要大约 34 小时的工作时间，每架成本为 2,890 美元。 60 架受影响的美国飞机的总成本预计为 173,400 美元（不包括任何维修费用）。
该机构表示，缺乏足够的信息来估计如果发现缺陷可能需要的纠正工作的成本。一些费用可以由波音公司的保修范围覆盖。
该指令遵循 FAA 于 2026 年 2 月 24 日发布的提案。在公众意见征询期间，波音和美国航空要求更改维修要求。
波音公司要求美国联邦航空局允许使用现有批准的程序进行维修，而不是要求每次维修都单独批准。美国联邦航空局同意了。
美国航空要求美国联邦航空管理局澄清密封剂需要在哪里进行测试，以及是否可以使用现有的波音维修程序。美国联邦航空局明确了检查区域，并同意允许现有的维修程序。
航空安全基金会单独询问波音公司现在是否在生产过程中执行所需的密封剂检查。
美国联邦航空局表示，该指令适用于没有足够证据证明检查已完成的飞机。它确认，在该指令范围之外的飞机生产过程中正在执行所需的检查。

title_en: Why 17 Regional Gates Matter So Much To The Airline Carrying Over 60% Of Miami's Passengers
title_zh: 为什么17个地区登机口对承载迈阿密60%以上乘客的航空公司如此重要
summary: Miami International Airport is one of the country's primary international gateways.
summary_zh: 迈阿密国际机场是该国主要的国际门户之一。
body_en: Journalist - Steven has a varied background in communications, and it was this passion for writing combined with his in-depth knowledge of the aviation industry that led him to Simple Flying. A keen linguist, he also has experience in translation and interpreting. Based in Palma, Spain

Miami International Airport (MIA) is preparing for a major transformation, and one of its most important developments involves an area that many passengers would rather forget. The $1 billion D60 expansion will replace an outdated regional boarding facility at Concourse D with 17 traditional contact gates, bringing an end to the bus transfers and outdoor boarding arrangements that have long characterized this part of the airport.

While the investment is substantial, its significance extends well beyond improving the appearance of a boarding area. For American Airlines , which carries more than 60% of Miami International Airport's passengers, the project represents an important investment in the infrastructure supporting its largest international gateway .

With approximately 400 daily departures from Miami, the airline depends on the airport to connect passengers across the US, Latin America, the Caribbean, and Europe. Improving just 17 gates could therefore have considerable consequences for its operations, passenger experience, and future growth.
Why Miami Is So Important To American Airlines

Miami International Airport occupies a particularly important position in American Airlines' network. Unlike many other major American airports, Miami provides the oneworld carrier with an extensive collection of connections to destinations throughout Latin America and the Caribbean.

Its geographical position makes it a natural gateway for passengers traveling between the US and numerous international markets, giving the airline a substantial competitive advantage in the region. American Airlines operates approximately 400 daily departures from Miami International Airport, making the airport one of its most important operational bases.

Its presence is also reflected in its passenger market share, with the airline carrying more than 60% of the airport's traffic. This concentration means that improvements to Miami's infrastructure have an especially direct impact on American Airlines compared with smaller operators using the airport. The largest airlines at Miami International Airport by market share, as per data from the US Bureau of Transportation Statistics , are outlined in the table below.

The importance of the hub is also connected to the wider economic significance of Miami International Airport. The airport handled 55.3 million passengers in 2025, ranking it among the busiest airports in the US. According to Miami-Dade County, its economic activity generates approximately $212 billion in business revenue annually and supports nearly 946,000 jobs.

This demonstrates how closely aviation is connected to the surrounding region's prosperity. For American Airlines, maintaining a strong position at Miami International Airport is therefore about considerably more than operating a large number of flights.

The airport supports connections between domestic markets and destinations across the Caribbean and Latin America, while also providing opportunities to attract international travelers connecting through the US. Infrastructure that accommodates growing passenger numbers is essential if the airline wants to preserve and strengthen this position.

The current D60 facility is unusual compared with the conventional boarding arrangements passengers experience elsewhere at major international airports. Rather than providing individual boarding areas connected directly to aircraft through passenger boarding bridges, the existing arrangement uses a shared boarding space serving 17 ground-level regional aircraft positions.

Passengers must consequently follow a less convenient process to reach their aircraft. For travelers, this can mean leaving the terminal building and boarding a bus before being transported to an aircraft parked outside the main concourse. In other circumstances, passengers use outdoor boarding arrangements, exposing them to Miami's heat, humidity and unpredictable weather.

Although such procedures are not unusual at airports serving regional aircraft, they are increasingly difficult to justify at a major international gateway. The shared boarding arrangement also creates practical challenges during busy operating periods. Passengers traveling on different flights must use the same general waiting area.

This makes the environment potentially crowded and confusing when several departures are approaching simultaneously. Managing boarding announcements, passenger movements, and flight delays becomes more complicated when multiple aircraft depend on a common facility rather than separate gate areas.

These limitations are particularly noticeable given the scale of American Airlines' Miami operation. An airport handling tens of millions of passengers annually needs facilities capable of supporting consistent passenger flows, including during peak departure periods.

The existing regional facility represents an increasingly outdated part of an otherwise extensive hub, making its redevelopment an important step towards improving the overall experience. American Airlines' regional flights are operated under the American Eagle brand. The carrier's regional subsidiary's flights are operated by the aircraft detailed in the table above, according to data from ch-aviation .

The D60 expansion will transform the existing regional boarding area into a three-level extension of Concourse D. Rather than simply renovating the shared waiting space, the project will convert the 17 ground-level regional aircraft positions into 17 traditional contact gates, each featuring its own passenger hold room.

This will provide a considerably more conventional boarding experience for passengers departing from the facility. The new gates will be designed to accommodate larger regional aircraft and narrowbody aircraft, providing greater flexibility than the existing arrangement. This is particularly important for American Airlines because aircraft requirements can change as passenger demand develops across individual routes.

The ability to accommodate different aircraft types gives the airline additional options when allocating capacity and planning its future operations. Passenger facilities will also receive considerable attention. Each gate will have an individual boarding area, while the expansion will introduce additional dining and shopping opportunities.

title_en: Ill-Fated Learjet Had Altitude Struggles Amid Severe Turbulence 6 Months Ago, ATC Audio Shows
title_zh: 命运多亏的Learjet在6个月前的严重湍流中进行了海拔挣扎， ATC音频节目
summary: Resurfaced ATC audio reveals a Learjet struggled with severe turbulence six months before its fatal crash in South Florida.
summary_zh: 重新浮出水面的ATC音频显示，一架Learjet在南佛罗里达致命坠机前六个月在严重的湍流中挣扎。
body_en: Paul has had a career of 25+ years focused on the international technology sector, which has taken him to over 100 countries. Along the way, he developed a deep love for aviation, with a travel bucket list measured by aircraft types flown rather than destinations reached. Now he brings that avgeek passion, along with the journalism experience he accumulated early in his career, to write insightful pieces for Simple Flying.

The Learjet 60 that crashed in Florida on Sunday , killing all nine people onboard, had experienced a troubling encounter with severe turbulence just six months earlier. Resurfaced air traffic control audio from May 2026 reveals that the same aircraft struggled to maintain its assigned altitude near Newark, New Jersey, prompting a controller to challenge the crew's description of the conditions as merely moderate turbulence .

The revelation, originally reported by the Daily Express , raises questions about similarities between the two incidents, particularly in how the pilots characterized the turbulence they encountered. Before Sunday's fatal crash, the Learjet's crew also reported moderate turbulence despite altitude fluctuations of up to 700 feet. However, investigators have not established a connection between the incidents, and the identities of the pilots involved in the May incident remain unconfirmed.
Learjet Crew Challenged By ATC After Unexpected Climb

The earlier encounter occurred in May, when the Learjet, registered as N722BD, was flying near Newark Liberty International Airport (EWR). According to audio obtained by The US Sun , a controller noticed the business jet climbing unexpectedly and questioned the crew. A female pilot responded that they were "just about to call you ," said they were experiencing moderate turbulence, and were unable to maintain their assigned altitude.

The controller immediately challenged that assessment and instructed the pilots to descend to 4,000 feet. The situation was particularly concerning because another business jet was operating nearby at a similar altitude, potentially creating a separation issue. A male pilot subsequently reiterated that the Learjet was experiencing moderate chop, but the controller insisted that an inability to maintain altitude indicated more serious conditions.
"If you can't maintain altitude, that's not moderate. That's severe turbulence."

The controller then explicitly asked whether the aircraft was encountering severe turbulence, prompting affirmative responses from both pilots. When questioned about possible injuries, the female pilot reported none, but confirmed that severe turbulence was continuing. The identities of the two pilots have not been established, and there is no confirmation that either was aboard the aircraft during its fatal flight six months later.
Why Severe Turbulence Can Make Maintaining Altitude Difficult

The May exchange highlights an important distinction in how pilots report turbulence. Under the Federal Aviation Administration's (FAA) turbulence classifications , moderate turbulence can produce changes in altitude, attitude, and airspeed, but pilots should retain positive control. Severe turbulence involves larger, more abrupt changes and can leave an aircraft momentarily out of position. The controller's concern was therefore consistent with established aviation terminology.
Slight, irregular changes in altitude or attitude
Changes in altitude or attitude, with positive control maintained
Large, abrupt changes; aircraft may be momentarily out of position
Aircraft violently tossed about; control practically impossible

This distinction matters in congested airspace, where aircraft must maintain assigned altitudes to preserve separation from other traffic. An unexpected climb or descent can create a potential conflict even when the deviation is caused by atmospheric conditions rather than pilot action. Accurate turbulence reports also help controllers warn following aircraft and coordinate alternative altitudes. However, difficulty maintaining altitude does not automatically establish a mechanical problem or loss of control.

For N722BD, the May recording indicates that the aircraft deviated up to 700 feet above and 400 feet below its assigned altitude of 4,000 feet. That suggests that the initial description of a "moderate chop" significantly understated the difficulties the crew was experiencing, and supports the controller's assessment of severe turbulence.
Six Months Later, The Same Learjet Crashed After Another Turbulence Encounter

N722BD departed Austin Bergstrom International Airport (AUS), bound for North Eleuthera Airport (ELH) in the Bahamas, carrying seven passengers and two pilots. While crossing South Florida at 35,000 feet, the crew reported light clear icing and turbulence, with altitude deviations of approximately 600-700 feet. The similarities to May are striking: once again, pilots aboard the same aircraft described "moderate turbulence" while experiencing substantial altitude fluctuations. Nevertheless, those fluctuations alone do not prove that the November conditions met the FAA's severe classification.

After encountering precipitation, the crew requested permission to climb to 37,000 feet, hoping to find smoother conditions. ATC approved the request, but less than 30 seconds later, the pilots reported an uncontrolled descent and declared an emergency. According to Flightradar24 , the aircraft's reported descent rate exceeded 32,000 feet per minute before it crashed in Palm Beach County, killing everyone aboard.

The NTSB investigation has already uncovered evidence of an inflight breakup, including pieces of the aircraft's left elevator found between 1.3 miles (2.1 km) and 3.8 miles (6.1 km) from the impact site. Investigators are examining weather, aircraft systems, maintenance records, and flight communications. Although both encounters involved turbulence and difficulties maintaining altitude, no causal connection has been established. A preliminary report is expected within about 30 days, and the final investigation will likely take considerably longer.

Premium economy on a London-New York flight can cost more than twice as much as an economy ticket, but the difference between the two cabins and business class can sometimes be surprisingly small. For passengers facing an approximately eight-hour transatlantic journey, a wider seat, extra legroom, better meals, and extra baggage can be appealing, but does the experience justify the added cost?

In 2026, passengers traveling between London Heathrow Airport (LHR) and New York JFK Airport have several airlines to choose from, including British Airways, Virgin Atlantic, American Airlines, Delta Air Lines, and JetBlue. Those flying to Newark Liberty International Airport (EWR) have fewer nonstop options, primarily British Airways and United Airlines . With different premium economy products, competing fares, and varying baggage allowances, how much should passengers actually expect to pay for a more comfortable transatlantic journey?
How Much Does Premium Economy Cost Between London And New York?

Premium economy on the London-New York route typically costs approximately $1,000 to $1,300 for a return journey, compared with around $500 to $600 for a standard economy ticket. This means passengers can expect to pay roughly twice as much for the upgraded cabin, although the difference depends on the airline, travel dates, departure airport, and availability.

According to our analysis of premium economy fares in 2026 , the transatlantic market demonstrates how airlines position their intermediate cabin between standard economy and business class. Premium economy has become a major revenue opportunity for carriers, letting them charge more for added comfort without offering the considerably more expensive lie-flat seating associated with business class.

However, the difference between cabins isn't always consistent. A NerdWallet comparison of British Airways fares found that one evening departure from New York JFK to London offered premium economy for $1,162, more than twice the $532 economy fare. Business class was available for just $1,222, meaning passengers would have saved only $60 by selecting premium economy instead. Another comparison showed a return premium economy fare of $1,459 against $737 in economy. These examples raise an important question: how much competition exists between airlines on the route, and where can passengers find the best selection?
Which Airlines Offer Premium Economy Between Heathrow And New York?

The greatest selection of nonstop services is available between London Heathrow and New York JFK. According to FlightConnections , five airlines serve the route: British Airways , Virgin Atlantic , American Airlines , Delta Air Lines , and JetBlue . The route covers approximately 3,440 miles (5,536 kilometers), with flights generally taking around eight hours.

However, passengers should distinguish between the airlines operating the route and those offering a dedicated premium economy cabin. British Airways calls its intermediate product World Traveller Plus, Virgin Atlantic markets its cabin as Premium, and American Airlines offers Premium Economy on eligible long-haul aircraft. Delta also operates Premium Select on eligible international services. JetBlue, meanwhile, offers its Mint business class and Even More Space economy seating rather than a conventional dedicated premium economy cabin.

The situation is different for passengers traveling to Newark. According to FlightConnections' LHR-EWR route information , British Airways and United Airlines operate nonstop flights between the two airports: United's intermediate product corresponding to British Airways’ World Traveller Plus is called Premium Plus. The route covers approximately 3,454 miles (5,559 km), with an average flight time of seven hours and 55 minutes.
British Airways, Virgin Atlantic, American, Delta, JetBlue
World Traveller Plus, Premium, Premium Economy, Premium Select

Such a variety of airlines at JFK makes it attractive to travelers seeking schedule flexibility and competitive fares. Nevertheless, more airline options do not automatically mean cheaper premium economy tickets. British Airways and Virgin Atlantic offer useful examples of what passengers can expect to pay.
How Much Do British Airways And Virgin Atlantic Charge For Premium Economy?

British Airways and Virgin Atlantic are two of the most prominent competitors on the London-New York market , and both offer dedicated premium economy cabins on their long-haul services. Their current fares demonstrate that passengers departing London can sometimes find considerably more attractive prices than those booking an equivalent journey from the United States .

Virgin Atlantic's official website provides a particularly useful snapshot of its pricing. For a return journey from London Heathrow to New York JFK between November 17 and November 22, 2026, the airline advertised Premium fares starting at approximately $1,529. Its published offers for selected dates in May, July, and August 2027 also showed starting fares of approximately $1,542 to $1,549. These are advertised starting prices, not guaranteed fares for every departure.

The airline's official Premium flight deals page also provides information about its cabin and included services. British Airways, meanwhile, allows passengers to compare World Traveller Plus fares through its official website .

Furthermore, the KAYAK sample for February 5–12, 2027 provides another useful comparison point during low season, with prices slightly lower than those for immediate departures within two weeks, although those dates fall outside the 2026 calendar year. With the fares set, the next question is what passengers get for spending more than £1,000 on a return ticket.

title_en: Defiant Ritz-Carlton Singapore Joining Marriott Bonvoy… Finally!
title_zh: Defiant新加坡丽思卡尔顿酒店加入万豪旅享家……终于来了！
summary: The Ritz-Carlton Millenia Singapore, the only Ritz-Carlton outside Marriott Bonvoy, will finally join the program on December 1, 2026, letting members earn points and redeem them.

body_en: The world’s only Ritz-Carlton that doesn’t participate in the Marriott Bonvoy program will finally be joining, which seems long overdue. I can’t imagine the hotel will be particularly generous, but we’ll see!
Ritz-Carlton Singapore joins Bonvoy as of December 2026

The 608-key Ritz-Carlton Millenia Singapore will be joining the Marriott Bonvoy program as of December 1, 2026. So as of that date, Bonvoy members will be able to earn and redeem points, and take advantage of Bonvoy elite perks, when staying at the hotel (admittedly Bonvoy elite perks at Ritz-Carlton properties are fairly limited, as breakfast isn’t a benefit for any elite tier ).

As I covered in late 2025, this property is the only Ritz-Carlton in the world that doesn’t participate in the Bonvoy program . The backstory here is that the hotel opened back in 1996, and at the time, Ritz-Carlton didn’t have any sort of a loyalty program that awarded points.

In 2010, the Ritz-Carlton Rewards program started awarding points for hotel stays, as a parallel program to Marriott Rewards. The ability to earn and redeem points came at a cost to individual hotels, but it was intended to boost occupancy and average daily rates.

Initially, hotels had the option of whether they wanted to opt in or out of the program. Most hotels bought into the concept, though the Ritz-Carlton Osaka and Ritz-Carlton Singapore were the two hotels that opted out. The Ritz-Carlton Osaka eventually decided to participate, leaving the Ritz-Carlton Singapore as the only hotel that’s not participating.

Ultimately when the Marriott Bonvoy program formed as the combination of Marriott Rewards and Starwood Preferred Guest, the hotel could still stick to its legacy contract of not having to participate in the program. Clearly the owners of the hotel have now had a change of heart… or something!
Why are the Ritz-Carlton Singapore owners backtracking?

Obviously we don’t have any sort of an official explanation for the reason that this Ritz-Carlton property is finally backtracking. I can’t imagine that Marriott gave the owners an ultimatum, given that Marriott is known for letting hotel owners get away with anything, as long as they get paid.

My guess is that the competitive realities just finally caught up with this hotel — Singapore is an increasingly competitive hotel market, this is a massive hotel with 600+ rooms to fill every night, and the hotel is also a bit past its prime.

The truth is that loyalty programs exist for a reason, as they’re a great tool for getting heads into beds. Obviously the hotel will be on the hook for some additional loyalty fees, but I imagine this will make the hotel more appealing to people who otherwise wouldn’t have considered it.

I also have to imagine that even though the hotel did a decent job communicating its lack of participation in Marriott Bonvoy, I still suspect many guests didn’t realize this, and ended up being disappointed.

As of December 1, 2026, the Ritz-Carlton Singapore will be joining the Marriott Bonvoy program. This is the only Ritz-Carlton hotel in the world that hasn’t participated in Bonvoy, so this is great to see.

The backstory is that the hotel opened before Ritz-Carlton had a loyalty program, and then when a program was finally formed, participation was optional. Literally every other Ritz-Carlton in the world saw value in this… except this one, apparently.
Fortunately they’ve now come to their senses, or something, so it’s great to see that this will be changing.
What do you make of the Ritz-Carlton Singapore joining Bonvoy?

Home Saab Gripen Swedish Gripens patrol Polish skies with multinational NATO tanker support

Swedish Saab JAS 39 Gripen fighters supported the protection of Polish airspace for more than four hours during an operation reported by Poland’s General Staff on 3 November. The aircraft conducted patrol and protective duties, supported by an Airbus A330 MRTT tanker identified as MMF19, according to Polish defence publication Defence24, which reproduced the military’s statement. The number of fighters involved was not disclosed.

The deployment forms part of a two-month Swedish mission that began on 1 October. Aircraft from Blekinge Air Wing, F 17, operate principally from Sweden, with a smaller forward operating presence in Poland, under NATO’s Combined Air Operations Centre in Uedem, Germany. Their responsibilities include protecting the logistics hub supporting Ukraine and contributing to NATO’s integrated air and missile defence. The “fourth mission” refers to Sweden’s fourth NATO fighter deployment, not necessarily its fourth operational scramble.

The tanker adds a multinational dimension, including a Belgian connection: NATO’s shared MRTT programme comprises Belgium, Czechia, Denmark, Finland, Germany, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway and Sweden. Programme membership does not, however, establish which nationalities crewed this particular flight.

Other allied contributions extend beyond fighter patrols. Dutch Patriot systems and approximately 150 personnel are deployed in Poland until early December. Sweden plans to deploy its own Patriot unit with around 100 personnel from December to protect the Rzeszów logistics hub, with preparations for a possible extension into the first half of 2027.

While the supplied report quotes Colonel Carl Bergqvist describing protection against Russian cruise missiles, the official statements reviewed do not confirm a missile interception, weapons firing or an airspace violation during this particular sortie. The confirmed activity is a defensive patrol with aerial-refuelling support—not a reported combat engagement.

In late 2023, Hyatt and Parks Hospitality Holdings announced a collaboration that will expand Hyatt’s footprint in Mexico, with the development of four new properties. If you ask me, the most interesting of these is the new Park Hyatt Riviera Maya, which will also be the brand’s first all-inclusive property.
There’s now an update, as the hotel’s opening date has just been moved forward by a couple of months, and it’s now expected to open in the coming weeks.
148-key all-inclusive Park Hyatt Cancun basics

The Park Hyatt Riviera Maya , located in Cancun, Mexico, is now accepting reservations for stays as of December 3, 2026. The hotel was initially supposed to open in 2025, then it started accepting reservations for stays as of February 2027, and now it’s accepting reservations for stays as of late 2026.

Hopefully the current opening date sticks, but if you book in the first several months the hotel is open, don’t be surprised if we see an additional delay , or at least don’t be surprised if not everything is ready.

The 148-key property will have a first-ever concept for the Park Hyatt brand , as it will be all-inclusive. Admittedly this is pretty normal for the Cancun area, but still, it’s noteworthy for a brand like Park Hyatt.

Hyatt has been leaning heavily into the all-inclusive space in recent times, particularly through acquisitions. So while Hyatt has grown massively in terms of its number of all-inclusive brands, it’s surprising to see even a traditionally non all-inclusive brand get this kind of an experience.

I’m generally not a fan of all-inclusives, or at least historically haven’t chosen to vacation at them. However, after my recent Ritz-Carlton Yacht Collection cruise , there is something I really enjoyed about not being nickel-and-dimed for everything, given how expensive luxury hospitality has become in so many places.

When it comes to the dining outlets, they’ll include Beach Grill IK’AL (the beachfront restaurant with seafood and Yucatecan flavors), Bruma (the steakhouse), Nutre Kitchen (the all-day dining restaurant), Pool Bar Brisa (the pool bar serving drinks & light snacks), Patisserie Market & Cafe (the coffee shop), Living Room (the lobby bar).

Accommodations will range in size from 559 square feet (52 square meters) to 2,303 square feet (214 square meters), so they’re generously sized, as you’d expect. The decor looks nice enough, but not like anything special.
As you’d expect, the resort will have amenities including several pools, a full-service spa, a gym, and more.

Once open, this adds to a growing number of luxury points hotels in the Cancun area. Just recently we saw the opening of the St. Regis Kanai and Waldorf Astoria Cancun , so it’s nice to see Hyatt’s most luxurious brand also expand to the Cancun area. As a matter of fact, the Park Hyatt will be immediately next to the Waldorf Astoria (which also recently became all-inclusive, as it wasn’t initially).

The Park Hyatt brand is really growing in Mexico right now. We’ve seen the recent opening of the Park Hyatt Los Cabos at Cabo Del Sol , while the Park Hyatt Mexico City is expected to open in early 2027. Beyond that, we also saw the recent opening of the Alila Mayakoba , another good luxury option in the Cancun area.
Park Hyatt Riviera Maya all-inclusive rates & points requirements

With the Park Hyatt Riviera Maya now bookable, what are rates like? If paying cash, rooms seem to generally start at around $1,500 per night, but that does include taxes & fees. So it’s obviously very expensive, but given Mexico’s high taxes & fees, it’s actually not quite as crazy as some may have expected.

Then again, I’m not necessarily expecting this to be typical Park Hyatt quality, given the extent to which this is outside the typical Park Hyatt wheelhouse. Oddly, at least as of now, rates seem to be the same whether one or two people are staying, which is unusual for an all-inclusive.
If you are looking to book a cash stay here, I’d recommend doing so through the Hyatt Privé program , which offers extra perks like room upgrades, a hotel credit, and more.
When redeeming points, the hotel follows World of Hyatt’s Category F all-inclusive award chart, which is the most expensive award pricing for all-inclusive properties.

Airlines regularly adjust their route networks, and Breeze Airways is no exception. The US low-cost carrier has been making several changes to its network recently. It has discontinued at least 11 nonstop routes since the beginning of this year. Most of these are domestic services connecting destinations in states such as Florida, Colorado, and New York.

However, the airline has also ended its service between Providence and Cancún , which was the Rhode Island airport's only international connection. Breeze had planned to resume the service on December 19, 2026, ahead of the Christmas holiday period, and continue operating until March 20, 2027. However, it has since removed all flights from its schedule, and the route is no longer available for booking.
Breeze Ends Providence's Only International Route

Breeze launched its first international service earlier this year in January, connecting Norfolk International Airport (ORF) in Virginia with Cancun International Airport (CUN) in Mexico. It subsequently introduced additional international routes throughout February and March. One of these was a weekly Saturday service from Rhode Island TF Green International Airport (PVD) in Providence to Cancún, which began in February.

However, the route was never intended to operate year-round. At the time of its launch, the airport described it as an eight-week trial scheduled to run through April, allowing Breeze to test demand before committing to a longer-term service. Indeed, the trial delivered disappointing results.

According to data from the US Department of Transportation (DOT), the low-cost carrier carried just 1,364 round-trip passengers on the route and recorded an average load factor of 49.8%, meaning fewer than half of the available seats were occupied. It also captured less than 11% of passengers traveling from Providence to Cancún.

Many continued to use connecting services or traveled to Boston Logan International Airport (BOS) for nonstop flights. Interestingly, Frontier Airlines previously operated nonstop flights between Providence and Cancún in 2022 and recorded a similarly low load factor of 50.2%.
Breeze Cuts Several Underperforming Domestic Routes

Although Breeze has expanded into international markets, domestic flights still account for the majority of its operations. It serves more than 90 destinations across the United States, focusing largely on underserved markets. However, not every route has attracted sufficient demand, and the low-cost carrier has discontinued several domestic services this year . In fact, some of those were fairly new.

One of those is its service between Washington Dulles International Airport (IAD) and Ogdensburg International Airport (OGS) in Upstate New York, near the Canadian border. Breeze launched the route in September 2024, but it recorded an average load factor of just 28.2% through July 2026, according to DOT data.
Average Load Factor (According to DOT, through July 2026)

Further ahead, the budget airline is preparing to end its nonstop service between Washington Dulles and Tri-Cities Airport (TRI) on November 30, 2026, less than a year after launching the route in December 2025. The service was introduced following a regional economic development initiative led by BRIDGE.

This raised more than $2 million in local funding to help attract Breeze to the Tri-Cities market, serving Johnson City, Kingsport, and Bristol. However, passenger numbers have remained relatively low. According to DOT data, Breeze carried 4,453 passengers on the route through July and recorded an average load factor of just 49.3%, equivalent to approximately 68 passengers per flight on its 137-seat Airbus A220-300 .
New Domestic & International Routes Are On The Way

While Breeze is withdrawing from underperforming markets, it is also preparing to launch several new routes. The airline has been particularly active in filling gaps left by Spirit Airlines . One such airport is Myrtle Beach International Airport (MYR) in South Carolina, where Breeze has become one of the largest carriers in terms of destinations served.

In February next year, the low-cost carrier plans to introduce nonstop flights connecting Myrtle Beach with BOS and Arnold Palmer Regional Airport (LBE) in Latrobe, Pennsylvania. It will also launch a service between Latrobe and Orlando International Airport (MCO). Notably, Latrobe lost its scheduled passenger services following Spirit's withdrawal.

Elsewhere, Breeze is expanding its international network from Tampa International Airport (TPA). The airline plans to introduce flights to Montego Bay, Jamaica, in December, followed by Santo Domingo, Dominican Republic, in June 2027. These will complement its new Tampa–Cancún service, scheduled to begin on December 18, 2026.
